diagnostic_evidence.quote: First notice  $1+\operatorname{Re}(\hat{\lambda} h) =\cos(\lambda h)$ provides $\operatorname{Re}(\hat{\lambda} h)<0$.
It is clear to realize $\operatorname{Re}(\hat\lambda h)>0$

issues.failure_explanation: When Re(λ)=0, λh is purely imaginary, so cos(λh)=cosh(Im(λh))≥1 and sin(λh)=i·sinh(Im(λh)) is not real. The real and imaginary parts of e^{λh} are cos(Im(λh)) and sin(Im(λh)), not cos(λh) and sin(λh). With the written formula, 1+Re(λ̂h)=cosh(Im(λh))≥1 gives Re(λ̂h)≥0, the opposite of the claimed <0. The same error appears in the Backward Euler proof of Corollary thm:be_cons and the RK2 part of Corollary thm:rk_cons, in each case inverting the inferred sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace cos(λh) with cos(Im(λh)) and sin(λh) with sin(Im(λh)) in each affected proof where the real and imaginary parts of e^{λh} are extracted. After this correction the inferences yield the stated conclusions without further changes.
issues.overall_effect: The proofs of Corollaries thm:fe_cons, thm:rk_cons (RK2 part), and thm:be_cons (Backward Euler part) are invalid as written because the trigonometric formulas for decomposing e^{λh} are wrong and yield the opposite sign in each key inference. The stated conclusions are correct with the right formulas but are not established by the proofs.
issues.title: Wrong trigonometric decomposition of e^{λh} in conservative-case proofs
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, routine substitution of the correct trigonometric arguments in three proofs. Every substantive claim and guarantee of the corollaries is preserved; no new lemma or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \operatorname{Im}(\hat{\lambda}h) = 2\operatorname{Im}\left(\dfrac{e^{-\lambda h/2}- e^{\lambda h/2}}{e^{-\lambda h/2} + e^{\lambda h/2}}\right) = 4 \tan\left(\dfrac{\operatorname{Im}(\lambda h))}{2}\right).

issues.failure_explanation: Solving (1+λ̂h/2)/(1−λ̂h/2)=e^{λh} gives λ̂h = 2(e^{λh}−1)/(e^{λh}+1) = 2tanh(λh/2), not 2(1−e^{λh})/(1+e^{λh}) = −2tanh(λh/2). Propagating the sign error yields Im(λ̂h)=−2tan(θ/2) where θ=Im(λh), but the proof claims 4tan(θ/2). The computed expression contradicts the claimed one, and the claimed expression does not match the correct value 2tan(θ/2). The sign-preservation conclusion happens to survive because both 4tan(θ/2) and 2tan(θ/2) share the sign of θ, but the proof's own computation (−2tan(θ/2)) reverses it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign in the algebraic expression to λ̂h = 2(e^{λh}−1)/(e^{λh}+1) and the factor in the imaginary part to Im(λ̂h) = 2tan(Im(λh)/2). The sign-preservation conclusion then follows directly.
issues.overall_effect: The implicit-trapezoidal part of the proof of Corollary thm:be_cons contains an internally inconsistent computation: the intermediate formula for Im(λ̂h) does not follow from the preceding algebraic manipulation. The stated conclusion Re(λ̂h)=0 and sign preservation is correct but is not established by the proof as written.
issues.title: Sign and factor errors in implicit-trapezoidal formulas within Corollary proof
issues.why_classification: Two local sign/factor corrections in one proof step restore a consistent derivation. All stated claims survive; no new argument is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes that all roots of 1+z+z²/2+z³/6 = e^{λh} have negative real part under the stated conditions on |e^{λh}|. This means Re(λ̂) < 0. The corollary statement claims Re(λ̂) > 0, which is the opposite. The table comp-table-one-step independently confirms 'Cond. Dissipative' (conditionally dissipative) for RK3 in the dissipative column. Direct numerical evaluation (e.g., λ = −1+i, h = 0.1) gives Re(λ̂h) < 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the inequality to Re(λ̂) < 0 for the RK3 case in Corollary thm:rk_diss, making the statement consistent with the proof and the summary table.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary claims RK3 learns an expansive (anti-damping) system from dissipative data. The proof and surrounding analysis show the opposite: RK3 learns a dissipative system under the stated conditions. The claim as stated reverses the mathematical conclusion.
issues.title: Sign error in RK3 dissipative conclusion (claims expansive instead of dissipative)
issues.why_classification: Although the repair is a one-symbol change, it reverses a formal result's conclusion from expansive to dissipative—a substantive change in meaning. The corrected claim is supported by the existing proof and table but the false claim of anti-damping for dissipative data is withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $a:=\operatorname{Re}(\lambda h)$ and $b:=\operatorname{Im}(\lambda h)$ denote the real and the imaginary part of $\lambda h$ respectievely.

issues.failure_explanation: The imaginary part of tanh((a+ib)/2) is sin(b)/(cosh(a)+cos(b)), using sin(b) where b = Im(λh). The proof uses sin(a) and sin(2a) instead of sin(b) and sin(2b), substituting the real part a into sine arguments that should contain the imaginary part b. With the wrong formulas and a < 0, sin(a) < 0 while sin(b) > 0, producing the opposite sign for Im(λ̂_exp) and invalidating the claimed sign-preservation. The stated theorem conditions were presumably derived from the correct formulas but the proof's 'direct computation' with the written formulas contradicts the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sin(a) with sin(b) and sin(2a) with sin(2b) in the imaginary-part formulas, then verify (or re-derive) the stated conditions on a and b to confirm they ensure sign preservation with the corrected expressions.
issues.overall_effect: The imaginary-part formulas in the proof of Theorem thm:added-1 are wrong, yielding the wrong sign for the extrapolated imaginary part and making the proof's sign-preservation argument invalid as written. The conditions on a and b in the theorem statement may also require re-derivation or verification with the correct formulas.
issues.title: Wrong variable in imaginary-part formulas of Richardson extrapolation proof
issues.why_classification: Correcting the formulas is local, but the conditions on the parameters may need nontrivial re-derivation to confirm sufficiency with the corrected expressions. The sign-preservation conclusion survives under comparable but potentially adjusted hypotheses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If a root $\zeta_j$ has a multiplicity $\mu$, then the general solution will include terms of the form
\[
n^{\nu}\zeta_j^n,~~~\nu=0,1,2,\cdots, \mu-1.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The condition |z_n(λ̂h)| ≡ 1 constrains only the excited solution component. The general solution z_n = Σ c_j ζ_j^n with exact data has c_j = 0 for all roots except ζ_1 = e^{λh}, so |z_n| ≡ 1 holds regardless of the moduli of the remaining k−1 roots. The inference |z_n| ≡ 1 ⟹ λ̂h ∈ ∂R_A (meaning all roots have |ζ_j| ≤ 1 with at least one on the unit circle) is not justified: unexcited roots could lie outside the unit disc. A nontrivial argument showing all characteristic roots satisfy |ζ_j| ≤ 1 is missing.

failure_location.quote: Since $\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)=0$, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:lmm},  $|z_n(\hat\lambda h)|\equiv 1.$ This means $\hat\lambda h\in \partial \mathcal{R}_A.$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a nontrivial argument (method-by-method or general) showing that all roots of π_{λ̂h}(z) = ρ(z) − λ̂h κ(z) satisfy |ζ_j| ≤ 1 when λ̂h = ρ(e^{λh})/κ(e^{λh}) with |e^{λh}| = 1, with at least one root on the unit circle.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the learned parameter lies on the boundary of the absolute stability region for conservative data is unproven. Downstream qualitative statements about stability of the learned discrete dynamics rely on this boundary property and are correspondingly unreliable.
issues.title: Invalid inference in proof that learned LMM parameter lies on stability-region boundary
issues.why_classification: The conclusion appears correct (verified for AB2, BDF2, AM3, Leap-Frog) but requires a nontrivial new argument not present in the source. The result is recognizably preserved once such an argument is supplied.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
A straightforward calculation shows that this inequality holds precisely when either
    \[
        \operatorname{Re} (\lambda^{*}h) <0
        \quad\text{or}\quad
        \lambda^{*}h\in[-i,i].
    \]

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims that |λ*h − √(1+(λ*h)²)| ≤ 1 holds precisely when Re(λ*h) < 0 or λ*h ∈ [−i,i]. This characterization is wrong in both directions. For z = 1 (with the principal branch), |1 − √2| ≈ 0.41 < 1 but Re(1) > 0 and 1 ∉ [−i,i]. For z = −1, |−1 − √2| ≈ 2.41 > 1 but Re(−1) < 0. More fundamentally, since ζ₁ζ₂ = −1, one root always has modulus ≤ 1 (after appropriate labeling), so |ζ₂| ≤ 1 is automatically satisfied and imposes no constraint on λ*h. A concrete counterexample: with Re(λ) < 0 and Im(λh) near π (e.g., λh = −0.1 + πi), the noise-free minimizer λ̂h = sinh(λh) has positive real part, and for large N the noisy minimizer λ*h is nearby, violating the claimed conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis |Im(λh)| < π/2 (or equivalently cos(Im(λh)) > 0), under which Re(sinh(λh)) = sinh(Re(λh))·cos(Im(λh)) < 0 and the claimed admissible region is correct. Alternatively, replace the false characterization with a correct description of the admissible set.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's claim that λ*h lies in {Re(z) < 0} ∪ [−i,i] is false in general. The result fails for parameter regimes where cos(Im(λh)) < 0 (i.e., |Im(λh)| > π/2). The c₁ = 0 part of the conclusion (elimination of the spurious root) is correct.
issues.title: False characterization of admissible region for Leap-Frog noisy minimizer
issues.why_classification: The fix requires adding a nontrivial hypothesis that excludes an advertised regime (|Im(λh)| > π/2). Under the restricted scope the conclusion is recognizably comparable and no new proof architecture is needed, placing it above minor but below serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The listed α coefficients (−1, 0, 1) give ρ(z) = z² − 1 and yield Σ jαⱼ = 2 but Σ βⱼ = 1, violating the first-order consistency condition ρ'(1) = σ(1). The resulting method is inconsistent (order 0) and does not approximate any ODE. The standard AM3 has α = (0, −1, 1), giving ρ(z) = z² − z and consistent coefficients. The formula in the two-step-methods analysis section (attributed to 'AM2') uses ρ(ζ) = ζ² − ζ, which matches the correct AM3, confirming the table error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the AM3 row to α = (0, −1, 1) and β = (−1/12, 2/3, 5/12), making the method consistent and matching the standard third-order Adams–Moulton scheme used implicitly in the analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The table defines AM3 as an inconsistent method. Using these coefficients to construct the characteristic polynomial or stability region yields incorrect results. The paper's analysis and corollary conclusions are correct for the standard AM3 but not for the table's version.
issues.title: Inconsistent AM3 coefficients in LMM coefficient table
issues.why_classification: The correction changes the mathematical definition of the AM3 method from an inconsistent to a consistent scheme. Although the fix is confined to one table row, it alters which method is being analyzed and requires verifying consistency—beyond a purely local typo fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: These conclusions follow directly from the Taylor expansion of $\dfrac{\rho(e^{\lambda h})}{\kappa(e^{\lambda h})}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Taylor expansion of ρ(e^{λh})/κ(e^{λh}) gives |λh − λ̂h| = O(h^{p+1}) where p is the method's order. For ABk (k-step, order p = k): the rate is O(h^{k+1}), not O(h^{k+2}) as claimed. For AMk in the paper's numbering (k-step where AM2 has k = 1, order p = k + 1): the rate is O(h^{k+2}), not O(h^{k+1}) as claimed. The AB rate is overstated by one power of h (e.g., for AB2 the actual rate is O(h³), not O(h⁴)), while the AM rate is understated. The two rates are effectively swapped in the theorem statement.

failure_location.quote:
\item ($k$-step Adams-Moulton methods) $|\lambda h- \hat{\lambda }h| = \mathcal{O}( h^{k+1})$,
        \item ($k$-step Adams-Bashforth methods) $|\lambda h- \hat{\lambda }h| = \mathcal{O}( h^{k+2})$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the exponents: state O(h^{k+1}) for k-step Adams–Bashforth and O(h^{k+2}) for k-step Adams–Moulton. The Taylor expansion then directly supports both rates.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem overstates the convergence guarantee for Adams–Bashforth methods (claiming one order faster than actual) and understates it for Adams–Moulton methods. Any downstream reasoning that relies on the claimed AB rate is invalid.
issues.title: Convergence rates for Adams–Bashforth and Adams–Moulton methods are swapped
issues.why_classification: Correcting the swap weakens the advertised convergence guarantee for AB methods by one order of h—a substantive loss of a claimed rate—while strengthening the AM guarantee. The repair is local but necessarily loses mathematical content (a faster claimed rate) for AB methods.
